flows.trigger: The user enables online model sharing for the selected provider and endpoint, then sends a chat request.
recipients: OpenAI, Anthropic, or a user-configured compatible provider
flows.purpose: Generate a requested conversational response or device-action proposal.
flows.transport: HTTPS to a fixed provider endpoint or a user-configured HTTPS endpoint; loopback HTTP is allowed only for a local model server.
flows.retention: Provider-controlled; QC Remote does not assert a provider retention period.
flows.userControl: Per-provider-and-endpoint consent can be disabled in Privacy settings. Attachment bytes are transmitted only with the request to which the user attached them and are omitted from later conversation-history requests. Recognizable credential-bearing URLs are blocked before transmission.

flows.trigger: A development-build user enables online model sharing, configures direct Gemini access, and sends a chat request.
flows.purpose: Exercise the development-only Gemini adapter; this code path is compiled out of public builds.
flows.transport: HTTPS to Google's fixed Gemini API endpoint.
flows.retention: Google-controlled according to the development account and service configuration; not asserted by QC Remote.
flows.userControl: Unavailable in public builds; a development user must separately enable provider sharing.

flows.trigger: The user selects Antigravity, enables online model sharing, and sends a request.
recipients: The separately installed Antigravity CLI and the provider account configured in it
flows.purpose: Generate a requested response using the user's separately installed provider software.
flows.transport: Local child-process input followed by provider-managed network transport.
flows.executionBoundary: The CLI starts in a dedicated QC Remote working directory, which is not an operating-system sandbox. It runs with the signed-in user's Windows account permissions and any permissions configured in Antigravity.
flows.retention: Provider-controlled; temporary attachment copies are deleted after the request and stale copies are removed on startup.
flows.userControl: Per-provider consent can be disabled; Antigravity permissions and sign-in remain controlled by that installation. Attachment bytes are staged only for the request to which the user attached them and are omitted from later conversation-history requests. Recognizable credential-bearing URLs are blocked before transmission.

flows.trigger: A development-build user explicitly starts Google sign-in for Gemini API access.
recipients: Google OAuth, Cloud Resource Manager, and Gemini API services
data: OAuth authorization code and PKCE verifier
Google account session data handled by the system browser
flows.purpose: Authenticate the user and identify a user-selected quota project for Gemini API requests.
flows.transport: HTTPS to Google; the OAuth redirect returns through a temporary loopback listener.
flows.retention: Refresh credentials are stored using the platform credential facility until disconnected.
flows.userControl: The user starts sign-in, chooses a project, and can disconnect the account.

flows.trigger: A development-build user enables online model sharing and sends a chat request.
recipients: Google Firebase AI Logic, Gemini Developer API, Firebase App Check, and Google Play Integrity
data: model, SDK, runtime, app and integrity metadata
flows.purpose: Generate a response and protect the publisher's Firebase-backed API access from abuse.
flows.retention: Google-controlled according to the configured services and account tier; not asserted by QC Remote.
flows.userControl: Default-off model-sharing choice in Privacy settings.

evidence.contains: Allow messages, attachment names and types

flows.trigger: The user accepts the voice disclosure or enables voice processing, then starts voice input.
recipients: The operating system's configured speech-recognition provider
flows.purpose: Convert user-initiated speech to chat text.
flows.transport: Platform-controlled; it may be local or networked depending on the configured recognizer.
flows.retention: Controlled by the configured platform speech provider.
flows.userControl: Voice starts only on user action; Android adds a separate default-off voice-processing choice and both platforms expose disclosure controls.

flows.trigger: The user pairs with and enables a remote relay.
recipients: The user-selected relay operator and its configured OAuth authorization server
data: OAuth bearer token for remote clients
routed device commands and device-state responses with persistent hardware identifiers removed
flows.purpose: Route authenticated remote control between a client and the paired device host.
flows.transport: HTTPS for pairing and WSS for the device session; OAuth introspection uses HTTPS.
flows.retention: Deployment-specific and unresolved until the relay operator is selected.
flows.userControl: The user chooses the endpoint, sees a relay-operator warning, and can unpair or disable the relay.

evidence.contains: OAuth introspection endpoint must use HTTPS

flows.trigger: The user connects a device, controls it, or exports diagnostics.
recipients: No remote recipient unless the user separately enables a model or relay flow
flows.purpose: Provide local device control, preferences, troubleshooting, Windows user-requested diagnostic export, and Android local diagnostic display.
flows.transport: Local USB/MIDI, process IPC, and app-private storage.
flows.retention: Preferences persist locally; session chat and pending attachments are cleared with the running session or the app's clear control.
flows.userControl: The user controls connection, local settings, Windows diagnostics export, Android local diagnostics display, and conversation clearing.

evidence.contains: does not include advertising or analytics
